cards.prompt: Do the subtrees land before the essay publishes?
cards.context:
Round 5 decided salt now and subtrees later. The repository is public since today, so a reader who follows the essay will find a design where a hidden run of words is protected by its salt and not yet by its shape. That is sound: the salt closes the hole on its own, and the subtree work is about disclosure size and defence in depth. But the essay will describe the attack, and a reader may go looking for the repair and find half of it.

The cost of doing it first is not small: proof_data and verify are inside the proven core, so the seventeen proofs are redone.

options.label: Publish the essay now; the subtrees are a later cycle and the essay says so

consequences.text: The essay ships while the material is fresh, and saying openly that a decided improvement is not built yet is more honest than a repository that looks finished.
A reader who checks the code sees a design the essay itself calls second-best, and has to trust the prose that the salt is sufficient.

options.label: Build the subtrees first, then publish

consequences.text: The repository a reader opens is the design the essay argues for, with nothing to explain away.
Seventeen proofs redone before a word is published, on a project whose own premortem named 'the tool becomes the project' as its most likely failure.

title: notary, round 6: what ships before the essay does
